Aisha Khan: Quick FYI - customer priv-vpc-030 reported that after we applied stricter RBAC to tenant service accounts their audit_subjects started to show as 'system' instead of tenant principal. Likely mapping issue in token reviewer.
Marco Velez: Token reviewer update rolled at 09:03Z? that PR changed how we derive principal: PR https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/changes/2666 commit d3a9c11. If tokens are missing 'sub' claim we fallback to system. We need to fix mapping fallback to preserve tenant identity based on pod labels.
Aisha Khan: Affected window ~09:03-09:46Z. SIEM flagged missing tenant ids for ~45min. Impact: 0 customer-visible data leak but makes audit logs non-actionable.
InfraBot: NOTE - revert candidate: rollback token-reviewer to v2.7.2. Command: kubectl -n private-ops set image deploy/token-reviewer token-reviewer=ghcr.io/redwood/token-reviewer:v2.7.2 && kubectl -n private-ops rollout status deploy/token-reviewer
Priya Desai: Do we have automated policy tests that exercise token->tenant mapping? If not, add a test. Also we should add a pre-deploy gate that runs a synthetic audit pipeline to ensure tenant principals are preserved.
Aisha Khan: Rolling back now. Will follow up with a postmortem doc.
Marco Velez: Small followup: when rolling back, confirm the scrubber didn't permanently purge fields. If reingest needed, preserve buffers.
Priya Desai: Also add a lint rule for token reviewers that prevents silent fallbacks to 'system' for pod-scoped service accounts.
